ops.title: /usr/libexec/InternetSharing IS the NAT engine for Tart/vmnet shared networking on this host — never kill it; killing it drops all guests off the tailnet; recovery = NAT:Enabled=1 + per-guest graceful tart stop
ops.body:
**The 2026-07-14 hostname-rename incident's hard-won facts** (full detail in cc-notes note `53de1ee`):

- `/usr/libexec/InternetSharing` + `com.apple.nat.plist` `NAT:Enabled=1` is the NAT engine backing Tart vmnet *shared* networking on the Mac Studio host, despite `SharingDevices=[]` and the Sharing pane showing Internet Sharing off. It spawns on vmnet attach (only when Enabled=1) and its `com.apple.nat.plist` writes are vmnet's own doing — do NOT read them as a leftover from a session, and NEVER kill the daemon or set Enabled=0.
- Killing it cuts NAT egress for every guest at once: guests keep DHCP leases and look "running" in `tart list`, but all drop off the tailnet. Recovery (validated): restore `NAT:Enabled=1`, then graceful `tart stop <vm> --timeout 120` **per guest** (KeepAlive respawns each; a new vmnet attach alone respawns the daemon but does not fix previously-attached guests).
- The incident itself: mDNS conflict renamed host LocalHostName `yasyf-home` → `yasyf-home-2` at 2026-07-14 07:27; claimant transient, never identified. If it recurs: rename back via `sudo scutil --set LocalHostName yasyf-home`, arm `tcpdump -i en1 udp port 5353` + `/usr/bin/log stream --predicate 'process == "mDNSResponderHelper"'`; fallback suspect is the laptop `yasyf` (192.168.4.145). Rename audit: helper's `PreferencesSetName` log events.
- `pgrep -x InternetSharing`, never `ps aux | grep` — the grep matches your own command line.

Related: [[metal-reboot-survival]], [[host-serving-migration-2026-07]], [[zsh-log-builtin-gotcha]]
